title: Syntagma sacrae theologiae (Liber II Cap. 1 densify complete)
author: Ludwig Crocius
edition: Syntagma sacrae theologiae (Bremen: Berthold Villerian, 1636). VD17 14:684303C. SLUB id335860389. Liber II Cap. 1 De summo hominis bono COMPLETE (PHYS 331-mid-339 before CAPUT SECUNDUM).
blurb: Ludwig Crocius — Book II Chapter 1 Whether there is some highest good of man, from the 1636 Bremen Latin. Densify COMPLETE (PHYS 331–mid-339): Liber II title on man's end as citizen of God's kingdom / eternal beatitude; summum bonum given and eternal (Augustine); every thing has its end; perfection and beatitude; proportioned perfection; mortal vs eternal goods; Dionysius Carthusianus vs Scotus; Richard; Thomas duplex contemplation (via vs patria); five hypotheses; rational soul as informing form, spiritual, separable; immortality defined with Bernard, Nyssenus, Augustine, Ambrose. Cap. 2 starts mid PHYS 339 (De animae immortalitate). Liber I Cap. 1–11 COMPLETE.
era_note: Crocius wrote in the early seventeenth century as Reformed professor at the illustrious school of Bremen. This is not a patristic work. It is a public-domain Latin Reformed retrieval on the same Fathers-site pipeline. The 1636 Villerian folio is Public Domain Mark 1.0. Do not treat the site as ante-Nicene only.
first_english_note: No complete public-domain English of this 1636 Latin Syntagma was locked as reading text. This is a new rendering from locked Latin for Liber II Cap. 1 densify complete.

text_history.method: English follows the locked 1636 Bremen Latin of Liber II Cap. 1 densify COMPLETE, reconstructed from SLUB Dresden page images (PHYS 331–mid-339 before CAPUT SECUNDUM). Same-page OCR (tesseract lat + Vision) used as check. No modern English was copied. Liber I Cap. 1–11 COMPLETE (english files not modified this turn). Cap. 2 (De animae immortalitate) begins mid PHYS 339. No Internet Archive copy was located.
